mainTopic: How a doubtful מצורע brings his אשם and לוג of oil with a stipulation, and how the קומץ and seven sprinklings can both be done without breaking בל תקטירו
overview: This amud finishes a teaching about a person who is not sure whether he is a מצורע. He brings an אשם and says: if I am not a מצורע, it is a voluntary שלמים. Because of this doubt, it must follow the stricter rules of both offerings, including being eaten for only a day and a night. The גמרא first uses this to challenge the claim that רבי שמעון does not allow bringing קדשים to a state of פסול. It answers that helping a person become purified is a special case. Next it asks about the מצורע's לוג of oil. He declares the oil a voluntary offering if he is not a מצורע, so the כהן takes a קומץ, refills the לוג, does the seven sprinklings and burns the קומץ. The גמרא then asks when the קומץ is burned. Burning it after the sprinklings fails because the leftovers shrank, and burning it before fails because of בל תקטירו. רב יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי answers that the sprinklings are done לשם עצים, only as fuel and not as an offering. He supports this with a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The doubtful מצורע's אשם is eaten only a day and a night
steps.stepSummary: The quoted teaching about a doubtful מצורע ends by saying that his conditional אשם/שלמים follows the strict rules of both and is eaten for only a day and a night. This is thrown out as a challenge to the earlier claim about רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is not a מצורע, this אשם is a voluntary שלמים. That animal must be slaughtered in the north, its blood put on the thumbs, hands leaned on it, נסכים brought, breast and thigh waved, and it is eaten for only a day and a night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote about a person who isn't sure if he is a מצורע. The quote shows his offering being eaten for less time than a שלמים normally gets, and the גמרא uses that as a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שלמים may normally be eaten for two days and one night, but here it is limited to one day and one night like an אשם. That means some of the meat might end up נותר (left over past its time) when it didn't have to be. This seems to show that רבי שמעון does allow bringing קדשים to a state of פסול from the start, which contradicts the earlier claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering; here, the offering a מצורע brings to complete his purification
A voluntary peace offering
Putting the blood on the right thumb and big toe (and ear) of the מצורע
Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before slaughter
Waving the breast and thigh, done with a שלמים
Eaten for a day and a night only, the shorter time limit of an אשם

steps.confusionAlert: The offering is not being treated as a plain שלמים. Because we don't know which offering it really is, every stricter rule from either side is applied, and that is exactly why the eating time is cut short.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו – אָשָׁם זֶה שֶׁל שַׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה.
phrases.english: And if not, this guilt offering is a voluntary peace offering.
phrases.notes: "If not" means if he turns out not to be a מצורע. This is the end of a teaching the גמרא started quoting earlier.

phrases.english: And that guilt offering requires slaughter in the north,
and placing of blood on the thumbs, and leaning of hands,
and libations, and waving of the breast and thigh,
and it is eaten for a day and a night!
phrases.notes: A regular שלמים gets two days and a night, so this shortens its time. That shortening is the point of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָאו – אָשָׁם זֶה שֶׁל שַׁלְמֵי נְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a quotation begun before this section, which is brought as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי שמעון holds one may not bring קדשים to a state of פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limiting a possible שלמים to a day and a night reduces its eating time and risks making it נותר, yet the teaching allows this from the start.

steps.title: Helping a person become purified is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case of the מצורע is special because the offering is needed to purify the person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The מצורע case is an exception because he has no other way to become purified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against bringing קדשים to a state of פסול still holds in general. When a person's purification depends on the offering, the worry about shortening its eating time is set aside. The challenge is pushed off as a special exception, not a disproof of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixing a person; making him fit, here by completing his purification
Is different

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important exception: the need to help a person reach purity can override the general caution about bringing קדשים to a state of פסול.

phrases.english: Fixing a person is different.
phrases.notes: The "person" is the מצורע, who can't finish becoming pure without this offering.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case as a special exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצורע case shows that רבי שמעון freely allows bringing קדשים to a state of פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general rule stands. Only where a person's purification depends on it is the shortened eating time allowed.

steps.title: The stipulation works for the אשם, but what about the לוג of oil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the stipulation solves the problem of the מצורע's לוג of oil, since a שלמים has no לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the אשם, but what can be said about the לוג?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the same case. The stipulation handled the animal, but the oil still seems to have no solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם could become a שלמים if he is not a מצורע, because their procedures can be matched. A מצורע also brings a לוג of oil, though, and no oil goes with a שלמים. So if he is not a מצורע, it is unclear what the oil would be.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out well (for one part, but not another)
A measure of oil the מצורע brings with his offerings
What can be said? (asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: This works out well for the guilt offering;
but the log, what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח אָשָׁם, לוֹג מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the eating-time issue to a new problem in the same case: the oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: The stipulation solution in the doubtful מצורע teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The stipulation turns the אשם into a שלמים, but no oil goes with a שלמים, so the לוג has no status if he is not a מצורע.

steps.title: He declares the oil a voluntary offering
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that he also makes a stipulation on the oil: if he is not a מצורע, it is a voluntary offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: this לוג shall be a voluntary offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the man makes a stipulation on the oil too. If he is not a מצורע, the oil becomes a voluntary offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil can be donated on its own as a voluntary offering. So the לוג also has a backup status, just like the אשם, and the stipulation covers both items.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary offering, given by choice and not out of obligation
That he says (introducing his stipulation)

phrases.english: That he says: this log shall be a voluntary offering.
phrases.notes: He means: if I am not a מצורע. It's the same "if not" style of condition he used for the אשם.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a stipulation on the oil
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oil has no fallback status if he is not a מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: He stipulates that the oil is a voluntary offering if he is not a מצורע.

steps.title: A voluntary oil offering needs קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if he is not a מצורע, the voluntary oil requires קמיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he is not a מצורע, and the oil needs a handful removed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. If the oil is really a voluntary offering, it needs its own special procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A voluntary oil offering needs a handful (קמיצה) taken and burned on the altar. If that isn't done, the oil would not be treated properly as a voluntary offering.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Removing a handful to burn on the altar
It requires

phrases.english: But perhaps he is not a leper,
and it requires removing a handful?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא לָאו מְצוֹרָע הוּא, וּבָעֵי מִקְמָץ
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the לוג can be a voluntary offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A voluntary oil offering needs קמיצה, which a מצורע's לוג does not normally get.

steps.title: The קמיצה is done
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the כהן does take a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן actually takes the handful from the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the handful covers the case where he is not a מצורע. The problem is solved by doing that step too.

keyTerms.meaning: That he removes a handful

phrases.english: That he does remove a handful.
phrases.notes: The one doing it is the כהן.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The voluntary-offering procedure would be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קמיצה is in fact performed.

steps.title: A מצורע's oil needs seven sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects from the other side: if he is a מצורע, the oil needs seven sprinklings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he is a מצורע, and the oil needs the seven sprinklings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the opposite worry. If he really is a מצורע, the oil needs the מצורע's own procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע's לוג must be sprinkled seven times before ה׳. Doing only the voluntary-offering steps would leave out the מצורע steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת who needs purification
Placing seven sprinklings of oil

phrases.english: But perhaps he is a leper,
and it requires the placing of seven?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא מְצוֹרָע הוּא, וּבָעֵי מַתַּן שֶׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the opposite worry to step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he is a מצורע, the oil needs seven sprinklings, which a voluntary offering does not get.

steps.title: The seven sprinklings are done too
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the כהן does place the seven sprinklings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the seven sprinklings are also done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the קמיצה and the seven sprinklings are done. That way the oil is handled correctly whether or not he is a מצורע, just as the אשם was.

keyTerms.meaning: That he places (gives)

steps.whatToRemember: For a doubtful מצורע, the stipulation covers both the אשם (it may become a שלמים) and the לוג (it may become a voluntary offering). Every procedure from both sides is done, and the shortened eating time is allowed because it helps a person become purified.

phrases.english: That he does place them.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצורע's procedure would be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seven sprinklings are also performed, so both possibilities are covered.

steps.title: The לוג is now missing oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that once the כהן takes a קומץ from the oil, the לוג is no longer complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the לוג is now lacking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the plan from the earlier steps. If the כהן took a handful out of the oil, the לוג is no longer full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצורע's oil must be a full לוג. Step 6 said the כהן takes a קומץ from it, in case it is a voluntary offering. Taking the קומץ makes the לוג short, so how can it still be used for the מצורע?

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking; missing some of its required amount
A fixed measure of liquid; the מצורע brings one לוג of oil

phrases.english: But it is lacking!
phrases.notes: "It" is the לוג of oil. Taking the handful out in step 6 left it short of a full לוג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new difficulty with the combined procedure set up in steps 6 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כהן takes a קומץ from the oil and still uses it for the מצורע's sprinklings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצורע's oil must be a full לוג. Removing a קומץ makes it short, so it cannot be used.

steps.title: He tops up the לוג, based on a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The כהן adds a little oil to refill the לוג. A משנה supports this: if the לוג became short before pouring, it may be refilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brings a little more oil and fills it up. As we learned in a משנה: if the לוג became lacking before he poured, he should fill it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן simply adds a bit more oil to bring the לוג back to full. It brings a משנה to show this is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a shortage in the מצורע's לוג can be fixed, as long as it happens before the כהן pours oil into his palm. Here the קומץ is taken before any pouring, so refilling works.

keyTerms.meaning: A little bit
Poured (the oil into the כהן's palm)
He should fill it up

phrases.english: That he brings a little and fills it;
As we learned: if the log was lacking
before he poured, he should fill it.
phrases.notes: "Poured" means pouring oil into the כהן's palm for the מצורע's thumb and toe.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical fix backed by a משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A short לוג is ruined and cannot be used for the מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: A shortage that happens before pouring can be fixed by refilling, so the לוג is still usable.

steps.title: The handful needs to be burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if the oil is a voluntary offering, its קומץ must be burned on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another problem. If the oil turns out to be a voluntary offering, taking the קומץ is not enough; it must also be burned on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a voluntary oil offering, the קומץ is burned so the rest becomes permitted to the כהנים. So far the plan only mentioned taking the קומץ, not burning it.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning on the מזבח
Requires; needs

phrases.english: But it requires burning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further objection against the voluntary-offering side of the stipulation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plan that the כהן takes a קומץ in case the oil is a voluntary offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A voluntary offering's קומץ must be burned, not just separated. The plan has not dealt with that.

steps.title: He does burn it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כהן does burn the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly: yes, the כהן burns the קומץ on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as steps 6 and 8: whatever each possibility requires, the כהן simply does it. This short answer sets up the next question about timing.

keyTerms.meaning: Burns (on the מזבח)

phrases.english: That he burns it.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording: "he burns it."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Simply doing what the doubt requires
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קומץ cannot be properly burned within this arrangement.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן burns the קומץ as well.

steps.title: When is it burned? Burning after the sprinklings fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the קומץ is burned. If it is burned after the seven sprinklings, the remaining oil has already shrunk, and a קומץ may not be burned for remains that shrank.
steps.simpleTranslation: When? If after the seven sprinklings, then it is remains that became lacking between the taking of the handful and the burning, and we do not burn the handful for such remains!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 12 by asking about timing. This step tests the first option: burning the קומץ after the seven sprinklings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinklings use up some of the oil. That means the oil left over shrank after the קומץ was taken but before it was burned. The rule is that a קומץ is not burned for leftovers that shrank in that window, so this timing does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
The seven sprinklings of oil done for the מצורע
The remains left after the קומץ is taken
Taking the handful (קומץ)
The handful taken out to be burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The shortage here is not the one solved in step 10. That shortage came from taking the קומץ and was refilled. This one comes from the sprinklings, which happen after the קומץ was taken and before it is burned. That is exactly the window the rule forbids.

phrases.english: When?
If after the seven sprinklings,
they are remains
that became lacking between the taking of the handful and the burning,
and we do not burn the handful for them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a two-sided challenge against step 12 by asking about timing. This is the first side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 12 that the כהן burns the קומץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the burning comes after the sprinklings, the leftovers shrank between taking and burning the קומץ, and that blocks the burning.

steps.title: Burning before the sprinklings fails too
steps.stepSummary: The second option: if the קומץ is burned before the seven sprinklings, then once part has gone on the fire, offering any more of it falls under בל תקטירו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If before the seven sprinklings: anything from which a portion goes to the fire is subject to "you shall not burn."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the second option: burning the קומץ before the sprinklings. It shows that this timing also runs into a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that once part of an item has been offered on the fire, offering any other part of it falls under the prohibition of בל תקטירו. Sprinkling the oil afterward counts like offering it. So burning first and then sprinkling is forbidden, and both options seem blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: The fires of the מזבח
The prohibition "you shall not burn" (ויקרא 2:11)
Before

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has trapped the burning of the קומץ in a dilemma. After the sprinklings, the leftovers have shrunk. Before the sprinklings, בל תקטירו applies.

phrases.english: If before the seven sprinklings,
anything from which some goes to the fires,
is under "you shall not burn"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11. Doing the sprinklings after the burning counts like offering more of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided challenge begun in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 12 that the כהן burns the קומץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the burning comes first, the later sprinklings are like offering more of an item already partly on the fire, which falls under בל תקטירו.

steps.title: The later sprinklings are done as if for firewood
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי answers that the כהן does the later sprinklings with the oil לשם עצים, like something put on the מזבח only as fuel and not as an offering. That way בל תקטירו does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, the son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, said: he brings them up לשם עצים. This means the later sprinklings are done like something brought up only as fuel, not as an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 14: how can the seven sprinklings be done after the קומץ was already burned without breaking בל תקטירו?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תקטירו forbids offering more of an item once part of it has gone on the fire, and the sprinklings count as offering. רב יהודה says the sprinklings are done לשם עצים, like something brought up only as fuel and not as an offering. So the prohibition does not apply, and the source in the next step shows that bringing something up לשם עצים is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: that he brings them up (onto the מזבח fire)
for the sake of wood, meaning as fuel and not as an offering
the prohibition against burning certain things on the מזבח as an offering

steps.confusionAlert: 'לשם עצים' does not mean the oil turns into wood. It only means the act is not done as an offering, the way wood on the מזבח is just fuel.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
That he brings them up for the sake of wood.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the oil sprinkled seven times after the קומץ is burned. Those sprinklings count like something brought up just as fuel, not as an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the בל תקטירו problem raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the act: the later sprinklings are done like fuel, not as an offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling the oil after the קומץ is burned counts as offering it and breaks בל תקטירו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sprinklings done after the קומץ is burned are treated לשם עצים, not as an offering, so בל תקטירו does not apply.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's ברייתא: what can't go up as an offering can go up as fuel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק as forbidding only burning 'as a pleasing aroma', which leaves room to burn as fuel.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says: 'For a pleasing aroma' you may not offer it up, but you may offer it up...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that burning something as fuel is allowed. The ברייתא's sentence continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says leaven and honey may not go up 'לריח ניחוח', as a pleasing aroma. רבי אליעזר learns that only burning them as an offering is forbidden. Burning them another way, as fuel, is still allowed. This is exactly what רב יהודה needs for the oil.

keyTerms.meaning: a pleasing aroma, meaning a real offering to ה׳
offer up, bring up onto the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בל תקטירו depends on the purpose of the burning. The same item can be forbidden as an offering and allowed as fuel.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"For a pleasing aroma" you may not offer up,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:12, talking about leaven and honey.

phrases.english: but you may offer up

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב יהודה's answer in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That burning something on the מזבח as fuel, not as an offering, is allowed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אליעזר on ויקרא 2:12, 'לריח ניחוח'.
